opex.text: The Bank’s primary uses of funds include originations of loans, withdrawals of and interest payments on deposits, purchases of investment securities, and the payment of operating expenses. Also, when the Bank has more funds than required for reserve requirements or short-term liquidity needs, the Bank invests excess cash with the Federal Reserve Bank or other financial institutions. The Bank’s liquid assets at September 30, 2026 consisted of $49.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and $211.2 million in securities available-for-sale that were not pledged, compared to $10.5 million in cash and cash equivalents and $161.1 million in securities available-for-sale that were not pledged at December 31, 2025. Currently, we believe the Bank has sufficient liquidity to support growth over the next twelve months and in the longer term.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $668 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $697 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

The Company recorded a provision for credit losses of $2.3 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $2.1 million for the first nine months of 2025.

The Company recorded a p rovision for off-balance sheet loan commitments of $43 thousand and $220 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The Company recorded a provision for off-balance sheet loan commitments of $22 thousand and $164 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
Non-interest expense was $8.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $31.5 million for the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of $23.2 million, or 73.6%. The decrease was primarily due to a $25.9 million goodwill impairment charge recorded in the third quarter of 2025.

Non-interest expense was $23.8 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $49.2 million for the first nine months of 2025, representing a decrease of $25.4 million, or 51.6%. The decrease was primarily due to a $25.9 million goodwill impairment charge recorded in the first nine months of 2025.

nonop.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonop.text:
Non-interest expense was $8.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $31.5 million for the third quarter of 2025, a decrease of $23.2 million, or 73.6%. The decrease was primarily due to a $25.9 million goodwill impairment charge recorded in the third quarter of 2025.

Non-interest expense was $23.8 million for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $49.2 million for the first nine months of 2025, representing a decrease of $25.4 million, or 51.6%. The decrease was primarily due to a $25.9 million goodwill impairment charge recorded in the first nine months of 2025.

pretax.text: For the first nine months of 2026, the Company reported consolidated net income before preferred dividends of $3.3 million, or $0.37 per diluted common share, compared to consolidated net income before preferred dividends and goodwill impairment of $38 thousand, or $0.00 per diluted common share, for the first nine months of 2025.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The Company recorded income tax expense of $279 thousand for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $736 thousand for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in income tax expense reflected a decrease in income before taxes, excluding goodwill impairment, of $1.3 million between the two periods. The effective tax rate was 20.03% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a benefit of 3.18% for the third quarter of 2025.

Income tax expense (benefit) was income tax expense of $891 thousand for the first nine months of 2026 compared to income tax benefit of $54 thousand for the first nine months of 2025. The increase in tax expense reflected an increase of $4.3 million in pre-tax income between the two periods, excluding the $25.9 million goodwill impairment in the first nine months of 2025.

net.text: Net income attributable to common stockholders was $392 thousand during the third quarter of 2026, compared to net loss attributable to common stockholders of $24.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per common share was $0.04 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to a loss of ($2.86) for the third quarter of 2025.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to the Three Months Ended September 30, 2025

Net interest income totaled $9.9 million, representing an increase of $1.3 million, or 14.8%, from net interest income of $8.6 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase resulted from a $3.0 million increase in interest income, primarily due to a $1.7 million increase in interest income on available-for-sale securities, due to an increase in the average balance of available-for-sale securities, and a $1.7 million increase in interest income on loans receivable as a result of an increase in the average balance of loans receivable. These increases in net interest income were partially offset by a $1.6 million increase in interest expense on deposits, as a result of an increase in the average deposits balance. The net interest margin decreased to 2.64% for the third quarter of 2026 from 2.72% for the third quarter of 2025.

Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 Compared to the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025

Net interest income totaled $28.4 million for the first nine months of 2026, representing an increase of $4.0 million, or 16.5%, from net interest income of $24.4 million for the first nine months of 2025.

intro.text: Broadway Financial Corporation operates through its wholly-owned banking subsidiary, City First Bank, National Association, which is a leading mission-driven bank that serves low-to-moderate income communities within urban areas in Southern California and the Washington, D.C. market. City First Bank offers a variety of commercial loan products, services, and depository accounts that support investments in affordable housing, small businesses, and nonprofit community facilities located within low-to-moderate income neighborhoods. City First Bank is a Community Development Financial Institution, Minority Depository Institution, Certified B Corp, and a member of the Global Alliance of Banking on Values.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Deposits are our primary source of funds for supporting our lending and other investment activities and general business purposes.
We primarily rely on customer service and long‑standing customer relationships to attract and retain deposits.

Because our information technology and telecommunications systems interface with and depend on third-party systems, we could experience service denials if demand for such services exceeds capacity, or such third-party systems fail or experience interruptions.
In the ordinary course of business, we rely on electronic communications and information systems to conduct our operations and to store sensitive data.
Net interest income depends upon the relative amounts of interest earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities and the interest rates earned or paid on them.
